lessons.title: Oracle SBC objects
lessons.summary: Oracle Communications SBC, formerly Acme Packet, is configured with realms, interfaces, session agents, and manipulation objects.
objectives: Name the objects the 10.1 docs use
Attach a manipulation inbound or outbound
Leave element-rule syntax in the configuration guide

illustration.title: Objects you may name
illustration.caption: This is a vocabulary list from the documentation, not a command script.
rows: SIP service address on a realm

paragraphs: Oracle Communications SBC was formerly Acme Packet. A realm is the routing and policy context, a sip-interface binds a SIP service address to a realm, and a session-agent is a named next hop.

In this synthetic the inside address is 203.0.113.10, the sip-interface address is 203.0.113.20, and the session-agent toward the carrier is 192.0.2.40. The product documentation, not this lesson, prints the configuration fields for those objects.

A sip-manipulation is a named set of header rules. In-manipulationid selects the manipulation for messages arriving on a sip-interface or session-agent, and out-manipulationid selects the manipulation for messages leaving.
An element-rule targets part of a header and lives under a header rule. Its field names are in the HMR configuration guide. This lesson names the object and does not invent the fields.

lessons.title: Header rules run in order
lessons.summary: Oracle HMR header rules run in configured order. The 10.1 fundamentals page names add, delete, manipulate, store, and reject.
objectives: Put header rules in configured order
Name the documented actions
Leave the reject status code in the release guide

illustration.title: Order is the feature
illustration.caption: A later rule sees the message earlier rules produced.

paragraphs: The 10.1 HMR fundamentals page describes the actions add, delete, manipulate, and store. Reject also exists as an HMR action.
This lesson does not invent the SIP status code that reject sends. Read the release guide before you use reject. The lab uses delete, which removes the named header.
Header rules run in configured order. If a store rule needs the Server value, that rule has to run before a delete rule on Server.
The teaching rule in the lab is a header-rule named strip-server. It sets header-name Server, action delete, comparison-type boolean, and msg-type any.

paragraphs: The SBC Edge product page describes SBC SWe Edge and says the same software family includes SBC 1000 and SBC 2000. SBC Core is a separate family.
This lesson does not invent Ribbon CLI. Procedures belong in the admin guide on the documentation portal, and peer notes belong in the interoperability guides.

sections.h: A validation list is not a catalog
paragraphs: A public Ribbon document about Azure Communication Services names support on SBC 5110, SBC 5210, SBC 5400, SBC 7000, and SBC SWe for that validation. Those model numbers belong to that validation, not to a price list.
That list is a validation snapshot. It is not the full current price list and it is not a complete product catalog. Do not treat those model numbers as every SKU Ribbon sells.

lessons.title: AudioCodes manipulation in software 7.6
lessons.summary: Software 7.6 message manipulation is a table of Message Type, Condition, Action Subject, Action Type, and Action Value, assigned to an IP group.
objectives: Name the five table fields
Name the documented action types
Treat the menu as release-specific

illustration.title: 7.6 manipulation columns
illustration.caption: The menu that opens this table changes by release.

paragraphs: AudioCodes Mediant message manipulation in software 7.6 uses the fields Message Type, Condition, Action Subject, Action Type, and Action Value. Each rule is one row in that table.

Action types include Add, Remove, Modify, Add Prefix, Add Suffix, Remove Prefix, Remove Suffix, and Normalize. The syntax guide defines the values. This lesson does not invent a normalization grammar.
A manipulation set is assigned to an IP group inbound or outbound. The direction decides which messages the set sees.
The on-screen menu is release-specific. Open the 7.6 manual for the software you are running instead of memorizing a click-path from a different release.

sections.h: What is safe to copy from this course
paragraphs: On CUBE the defended line is request INVITE sip-header Diversion remove inside voice class sip-profiles. On Oracle the defended block is a header-rule with action delete.
On AudioCodes software 7.6 the defended row uses Action Type Remove and an Action Subject. Pasting the CUBE line into an Oracle header-rule does not configure either product.

CUBE applies the profile rules on the leg where that profile is attached. Oracle header rules run in configured order. AudioCodes uses the manipulation set assigned inbound or outbound on the IP group.
When a header survives, check those three attachments before inventing a fourth syntax. Ribbon procedures stay in the Ribbon admin guide and are not given a CLI here.

lessons.title: Identity at a trust boundary
lessons.summary: P-Asserted-Identity is a network-asserted identity. An SBC at a trust boundary decides whether that assertion continues.
objectives: Read P-Asserted-Identity and Privacy
Strip an assertion that arrives from an untrusted peer
Use the interop guide for header mapping

illustration.title: Trust boundary
illustration.caption: Add an assertion only for a peer you are willing to tell the identity to.

layers.name: Trusted egress
layers.detail: Assert only an identity you authenticated

paragraphs: RFC 3325 defines P-Asserted-Identity as an identity asserted by a network element. The synthetic carrier INVITE asserts sip:+15551212@example.com and sets Privacy: id, which asks downstream elements to withhold that identity.
An untrusted peer can put any URI in that header. Forwarding it onto the enterprise leg treats the carrier’s assertion as your own. The defensive action is to remove or replace it on ingress.
Diversion and History-Info are different redirecting headers. If one side sends Diversion and the other accepts History-Info, the mapping belongs in the interop guide for that pair.

CUBE profiles, Oracle header rules, and AudioCodes manipulation sets are the tools. Ribbon peer notes are in the interoperability guides. This lesson does not invent a Ribbon command or a universal translation formula.

lessons.title: Certificate names and Contact
lessons.summary: The certificate name and the SIP Contact need to be names the peer accepts. Teams and Webex Local Gateway do not share a wildcard rule.
objectives: Match a certificate name to the SIP name
Use an FQDN in a Teams Contact
Keep Webex Local Gateway off wildcard certificates

illustration.title: Wildcard certificates
illustration.caption: The same file can be acceptable to one peer and rejected by another.
rows: Certificate-based trunk for a third-party SBC
Read RFC 5922 and that peer’s guide

paragraphs: RFC 5922 describes domain certificates for SIP. The name in the certificate is the name the peer checks, and the SIP Contact on a TLS trunk should be the name that peer expects.
The synthetic Teams INVITE uses Contact sip:sbc@sbc1.example.com and Via host sbc1.example.com. The signaling port for Direct Routing is 5061 toward sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com.
Microsoft says wildcard names in the certificate CN or SAN are supported for Direct Routing. A Contact that is an IP address, such as 203.0.113.20, is not that pattern: the proxy returns 403.

The Webex Local Gateway get-started article says wildcard certificates are not supported for Local Gateway. A certificate that Teams accepts can still be the wrong certificate for a Webex Local Gateway.
